sentences.text: Vasco was ninety-one and lived in the house at the top of the lane and had not farmed the field in a dozen years.
He was hard to talk to.
Not unfriendly — he simply took a long time to arrive at a conversation, and if you filled the silences he would let you, and then you would have said everything and he would have said nothing.
Tomás had been coached on this by his father in the car and did the difficult thing, which was to state the situation in four sentences and then stop talking.
Vasco sat in his chair for what felt like a year.
Then he said: "By the concrete." "Yes." "How high." "About twelve metres.

Same place, four days." Vasco nodded slowly, twice, and then said something that Tomás did not follow at all, which was: "Then it's not a vole, and I'm too old to go down there, and you'd better take a spade." He would not explain further.
What he said, on the way out, at the door, in the tone of a man deciding to give away one thing and not two, was this: "My father used to say you don't look for a lost thing.
You look for what's paying attention to it."
